coveredBoundaries: Signed release pinned atomically to the allocation, offer and boot deadline; admission makes no provider request.
Idempotent admission preserves the original pin after the configured default changes.
Resolver and bootstrap renderer verify current release trust and exact provider snapshot ownership.
SQL rejects changed pins, substituted bootstrap images, second create effects and reversed retirement.
Cancellation before fresh IP/VM creation compensates and retires the allocation.
Unknown create holds snapshot ownership until original labelled server confirmation; permanently unknown create retains its pin.
Rejected create releases its pin only after IP compensation and retirement.
Untrusted post-admission or renderer-time image selection compensates; a busy image lock remains retryable.
Admission queues only deadline cleanup; explicit CLI start and real Graphile tasks advance to publication.
Retained expiry timestamp is persisted; cancellation cleans on the running worker; filesystem cleanup retries across a new connection.
Cancellation and retention scheduling serialize on the same build row.
Verifier lifetime uses database time with a five-second host-ahead test; release publication/selection pass with host clock ahead and behind.
failuresResolved: Post-admission release validation originally threw a plain Error; it now produces typed nonretryable failure and compensation.
Publication lock contention originally entered generic failure; retryable provider_unavailable now leaves progress for another tick.

A broad run exposed about two milliseconds of host/database skew at the verifier lifetime limit. The first DB helper assumed raw Drizzle timestamps were Date objects; it now requests numeric epoch milliseconds.
A subsequent full run found six failures from verifying DB-issued releases against host time. Signing verification, selection and admission now use database time consistently.
Adding the root Graphile dev dependency initially left an incomplete peer resolution; pnpm install --fix-lockfile repaired the lock and link. Final CI must confirm frozen installation.
limits: Image and customer provider operations here use protocol fixtures. Native enrollment uses real Smallstep/OpenSSH but simulated provider observations.
The real queue test checks retained expiry scheduling and actual cancellation cleanup; it does not wait a day for a provider retention deadline.
No paid Hetzner create, snapshot, boot, or deletion was attempted.
Optional internal image configuration supports unpublished-image fixtures. Production admission must require a release before live activation.
Production image worker/signing configuration, reachable enrollment, certificate renewal/recovery and the bounded Hetzner drill remain open.
Application deployment, routes, recipes, backups/restoration and self-hosting remain later milestones.
